sn47.42:1.1: This discourse, while doctrinally important, is textually corrupt. It appears to be a fragmentary stub of a text that is more satisfactorily preserved in the Chinese translation at SA 609.
sn47.42:1.3: This question appears rather oddly here. SA 609, rather, asks “What is the origination and cessation of the four kinds of mindfulness meditation”, then explains them, then rounds off by saying it has answered the question.
sn47.42:1.4: The same statement is said of “form” (_rūpa_) at [sn22.56:3.4]() and [sn22.57:2.4]().
sn47.42:1.5: While the specified origin and ending are the same, the Chinese text fills out each section by saying that one who meditates observing origin and ending will be independent and not grasp anything in the world. This passage is similar to one found in the Satipaṭṭhānasutta, but not elsewhere in the Pali ([mn10:5.3]()).
sn47.42:1.6: Also at [sn22.56:6.5]() and [sn22.57:6.6](). Here the plural form is specified.
